class.name: FlowSubgraphNode
class.brief_description: Runs another [FlowGraph] from its start node and continues when it ends.
class.description: The subgraph node reuses a graph inside another graph. It has the flow input [code]in[/code], the flow output [code]out[/code] and one flow output per name in [member exit_names]. When a [FlowGraphPlayback] enters it, the graph in [member graph] runs from its start node on a new graph level with the same blackboard. When that graph ends, the playback continues through the output named like the [member FlowEndNode.end_name] of the inner end node if that name is in [member exit_names], else through [code]out[/code]. A missing graph is a configuration warning; at runtime it stops the playback with an error, as does nesting deeper than [member FlowGraphPlayback.max_subgraph_depth]. [codeblocks] [gdscript] var subgraph := FlowSubgraphNode.new() subgraph.graph = preload("res://graphs/shop.tres") subgraph.exit_names = PackedStringArray(["bought", "left"]) graph.add_node(subgraph) [/gdscript] [csharp] var subgraph = new FlowSubgraphNode { Graph = GD.Load<FlowGraph>("res://graphs/shop.tres"), ExitNames = ["bought", "left"] }; graph.AddNode(subgraph); [/csharp] [/codeblocks]

members.member: Extra flow outputs, one per name. When the inner graph ends at a [FlowEndNode] whose [member FlowEndNode.end_name] is in this list, the node continues through the output of that name; any other end continues through [code]out[/code].
The graph to run. It is a separate resource and keeps its own nodes, variables and start node.
